node-1.label: Bilateral symmetric concentric ring-shaped opacities in posterior corneal stroma

node-2.label: Patient is a man in his 70s, presented for routine ophthalmic examination with no specific ocular symptoms, no history of eye surgery; annual physical exam showed no abnormalities with lipid and glucose levels within normal range.

node-3.label: Right eye examination: best spectacle-corrected visual acuity 20/20, normal conjunctiva and adnexa, cornea with normal luster and even surface, no distinct arcus senilis, normal anterior stroma; 4 symmetric complete concentric ring-shaped opacities in posterior corneal stroma, outermost ring ~4mm from limbus, vertical diameters 6.0mm, 4.8mm, 4.5mm, 3.6mm; ring surfaces smooth without deposits, pigmentation, or serrations; peripheral cornea with posterior crocodile shagreen; corneal sensations normal.

node-4.label: Left eye examination: similar findings plus small nasal pterygium; keratometry readings 43.4×43.4 D OD and 43.0×44.8 D OS; mild nuclear sclerosis of crystalline lens in both eyes.

node-5.label: Age-related posterior corneal degeneration (e.g., posterior crocodile shagreen)

why.why: In vivo confocal microscopy demonstrates long bandlike structures with thin streaks and no cellular infiltration, a characteristic feature of posterior crocodile shagreen. Combined with bilateral symmetric ring opacities on slit-lamp, asymptomatic late onset, and normal metabolic screening, this strongly supports an age-related posterior corneal degeneration; confidence increased from 0.75 to 0.88.

Normal lipid and glucose levels, smooth rings without deposits or pigmentation, and confocal microscopy showing no cellular infiltration or deposit-like structures effectively exclude metabolic deposition disease. The expert analysis also emphasizes that normal metabolic screening strongly supports a benign degenerative process; confidence lowered from 0.15 to 0.05.

Late onset, complete absence of symptoms, and confocal findings typical of posterior crocodile shagreen make an inherited deep stromal corneal dystrophy unlikely. Family history and genetic testing remain unavailable, so a small residual possibility is retained; confidence lowered from 0.10 to 0.08.

Confocal microscopy reveals no cellular infiltration, and slit-lamp examination shows smooth rings without vascularization, pigmentation, or inflammatory signs. Normal corneal sensation and an asymptomatic course further refute an inflammatory or infectious process; confidence lowered from 0.05 to 0.02.
